Sports.title: Why Jonathan David is playing for Canada and not leading the USMNT attack
Sports.content:
Tab Ramos attempted to convince Jonathan David to swap Canada for the United States in what could have been a move that changed USMNT's fortunes on the international stage.

Why Jonathan David is playing for Canada and not leading the USMNT attack

What has always felt like the missing piece for the United States men's national team could have been resolved long ago.

The lack of a world-class striker has historically acted as the ultimate glass ceiling for the USMNT on the global stage.



6 The lack of a true No.9 has plagued the U.S men's team Credit: Getty

This was exposed during the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, when the pool of strikers that included Josh Sargent and Timothy Weah underwhelmed.

The team's starting strikers combined for no goals on six shots - of which only one was on target - and an expected goals value of 0.50 over their four World Cup matches, according to OptaJack.

In the early 2000s, U.S. Soccer legend Tab Ramos - infamously elbowed out of the last men's World Cup on US soil - embarked on a huge recruiting mission.



If it had worked out, it could have changed the course of history for the USMNT.

Could Jonathan David have played for the USMNT?

Born in Brooklyn, New York, David moved to Haiti when he was just three months old, where his parents hail from.



Six-years later, he and his parents immigrated to Ottawa.

David was eligible to represent the United States, Haiti or Canada on the international stage, ultimately choosing the latter.

There, he would go on to rise up through the Canadian ranks, and Octavio Zambrano, a former manager of the international team, had a lot of conversations with the U-17 head coach about a call up to the senior team.



"We needed to lock him in for Canada," Zambrano told Farhan Devji in 2021. “So, I was really confronted with the idea of just taking him, not on the base of merit, to the Gold Cup.

“Just so I could put a jersey on him and debut him so he couldn’t play for any other team. We all knew that he had roots also in the United States. And it was a tough decision.

6 David rose through Canada's ranks despite having the opportunity to play for USMNT and Haiti Credit: Getty

6 Ramos, who had 81 caps for USMNT, tried to swoop in and get David to change alliances Credit: Getty



"But I couldn’t bring myself to take a spot from another player.”

"He was the one they were thinking about as a great player to bring into the national team," Zambrano continued.

Ultimately, David was left off the roster, which is when Ramos - who, at the time was the youth technical director for USMNT - eventually invited David to join the U.S. U-20 national team the following year.

But David respectfully declined, citing that his heart was always set on Canada.

Davis' domestic record proves what they missed out on

In his first appearance for Canada, David contributed two goals and an assist in a 8-0 drubbing of the U.S. Virgin Islands.



Moving from Canada to Europe in 2018, he joined Gent's youth setup where he was quickly promoted to the first team.

6 Ramos' plea didn't work, and David is now Canada's all-time leading goal scorer Credit: Getty

After 37 goals in 83 appearances, LOSC Lille shattered their transfer record, bringing David to France for €30 million.

In his first season, David formed a lethal partnership with Burak Yilmaz, scoring 13 goals in Ligue 1.



This included a legendary match winnera gainst Paris Saint-Germain to secure Lille's historic league title.

Over his five years in France, he proved to be an incredibly durable and elite volume scorer, racking up exactly 87 goals in 177 Ligue 1 appearances.

Across all competitions, he left the club as a modern icon with 109 goals, cementing himself as Lille's top scorer of the 21st century.

After running down his contract in France, David became one of the most coveted free agents in football, ultimately signing a long-term deal with Italian giants Juventus.



6 David's first season with Juventus wasn't his best. Credit: Getty

6 Folarin Balogun appears to have been the missing piece in the USMNT's frontline Credit: Getty

His first season under Luciano Spalletti didn't quite go to plan, managing just eight goals in 45 appearances across all competitions.

The USMNT, however, has since managed to close the recruitment loop by successfully convincing Ligue 1 breakout star Folarin Balogun to trade England for America, who has already notched two goals in this year's World Cup on home soil.



They also punched their ticket to the Round of 32 in dominant fashion, winning Group D before they even take to the field for their third, and final, group outing against Türkiye on Thursday, with their likely opponent being Bosnia & Herzegovina.

Meanwhile, David has showed up for Canada on the global stage, having notched a hat trick in their thumping 6-0 victory over Qatar in the Group Stages of the competition, albeit the win was overshadowed by a horrific lower leg injury to midfielder Ismael Kone.

The Canadians are also safely through to the knockout stages, finishing as runners-up behind Switzerland in Group B, with South Africa confirmed as their opponents.

Nonetheless, the miss on David's pedigree in front of goal could yet become the ultimate historical "what-if" hanging over manager Mauricio Pochettino's frontline, depending on how each country's progression in the World Cup goes.



Stay up to date on all things World Cup across our talkSPORT platforms - subscribe to our YouTube channel for the latest news, opinion, exclusive interviews and our daily unfiltered, unscripted show 'The S* Word, from 8am ET.

All 104 games at the 2026 World Cup this summer will be live on talkSPORT, talkSPORT 2 and the talkSPORT app.

Sports.title: Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana set for another loan move
Sports.content:
Andre Onana is close to sealing a new loan move to Trabzonspor, talkSPORT understands.

Talks between the Turkish side and Manchester United are at an advanced stage with all parties looking to finalise the deal, which doesn't include a buy option.



3 Onana looks set to depart United on a permanent transfer this summer Credit: Getty

The 30-year-old linked up with the Turkish side in September 2025 on a season-long loan deal.

His switch to Papara Park came days after he started in the Red Devils' humiliating Carabao Cup second round defeat away to League Two outfit Grimsby Town.

But despite making a howler shortly into his Trabzonspor debut, he ended up becoming a firm fan favourite.



Onana featured in 29 Turkish top-flight matches - keeping six clean sheets - to help his side finish in third spot.

And he also ensured it was a season to remember after lifting the Turkish Cup as he started in the 2-1 final victory over Konyaspor.



The ex-Inter Milan shot-stopper has recently seen his United salary receive an increase of around 25 per cent due to Michael Carrick's men securing Champions League qualification.

But while he regained form and confidence on loan, talkSPORT reported in May how they still plan to offload Cameroon international this summer.



Belgium shot-stopper Senne Lammens has been an instant hit at Old Trafford since arriving from Royal Antwerp on deadline day.

Summer switch

Despite rumours that Besiktas are looking to secure Onana's services, Trabzonsor president Ertugrul Dogan recently declared he is desperate to keep the player at the club.

He has already insisted that personal terms will not be an issue.

3 Onana featured 33 times for Trabzonspor during his loan spell across all competitions Credit: Getty

Dogan told Ajansspor: "I think Andre Onana will stay with the team, we've met his financial demands.



"The fans like him too, he's a decent bloke, I don't think we'll have any problems.

"I don't think he'll find the same level of interest in him anywhere else.

"So I think he'll stay with the team."

Should Onana depart United, he will follow a host of high-profile names already out the door.

It was confirmed earlier this month how striker Rasmus Hojlund, who joined alongside Onana in 2023, completed a permanent move to Napoli after his loan spell.



3 Onana's only appearance for United in the 2025/26 season came in the penalty shootout defeat at Grimsby Credit: Getty

Along with Onana and Hojlund, United also named six players that will be departing as free agents when their contracts expire at the end of June.

They include Casemiro, Jadon Sancho and Tyrell Malacia, while Marcus Rashford still faces an uncertain future after helping Barcelona win the LaLiga title during his loan stay.

Andre Onana's Manchester United career

Onana arrived at the Theatre of Dreams from Inter Milan in a £47.2million deal - one month after the Italian giants lost to Manchester City in the Champions League final.



But despite winning the FA Cup in his opening season in England, Onana was marred by consistent errors.

From his 102 outings across all competitions, he shipped in a whopping 150 goals - keeping just 24 clean sheets.

Sports.title: Ex-EFL player handed 11-game ban for racial abuse of teammate
Sports.content:
Ex-Watford midfielder Pierre Dwomoh has been banned for 11 games by the FA for racially abusing a teammate.

Dwomoh announced that he had left the Championship club in April – his ban is backdated to then.



2 Dwomoh made three appearances for Watford last season Credit: Getty

FA finds Dwomoh guilty

The 22-year-old Belgian was ruled by an independent disciplinary commission to have committed a 'very serious' and 'completely unacceptable' offence when he targeted an under-21 player of Indian heritage (referred to as Player A).

Dwomoh said the abuse had 'started just as a joke' when he was interviewed by the FA.

The offences in question are said to have taken place during the pre-match warm-ups before two U21 games last autumn.



One of the comments is understood to have been overheard by Watford’s leads sports scientist, Alisdair Walker.

Walker noted that Player A appeared 'bewildered' and 'did not seem himself' following the incident.



Watford subsequently contacted the FA alleging that a discriminatory comment had been made.

Watford back verdict

Dwomoh had previously been unhappy with Player A for not passing the ball to him, with it being acknowledged that Dwomoh 'may have been upset about this'.



In addition to the ban, Dwomoh has also been fined £2,500 and ordered to attend a mandatory training programme.

Confirming Dwomoh had been released, Watford told the Watford Observer they supported the FA’s decision to punish the player.

Watford signed Dwomoh from Belgian club Royal Antwerp in the summer of 2024.

2 Dwomoh joined Watford from Royal Antwerp two years ago Credit: Getty



He want on to make 12 appearances for the Hornets, who finished 16th in the Championship last season.

The Vicarage Road club recently announced the appointment of their 24th permanent manager in just 14 years, naming Italian Alessio Donisi as the successor to Edward Still.

Sports.title: Norway v France knockout phase permutations with Germany showdown in store
Sports.content:
Norway and France lock horns in the final round of Group I games on Friday night.

The European duo are already guaranteed a spot in the next round of the World Cup having won both matches so far.



2 Mbappe, like Haaland, has scored four goals at the 2026 World Cup Credit: Getty

As such, this showdown should be a bit of a dead rubber, right?

Well, not exactly.

Fans will bear witness to the goalscoring battle between goal machines Erling Haaland and Kylian Mbappe.

And their respective nations will hope Haaland and Mbappe can maintain their rich vein of form in front of goal at the World Cup.

The Norwegian hitman and his French counterpart are both locked on four goals apiece having hit respective braces against Iraq and Senegal.



What do France and Norway need to do to secure top spot in Group I?

There is now the chance to secure a round-of-32 spot as winners of Group I, though is it worth going all out to claim all the spoils in the Friday showdown?

For France, they only need to avoid defeat in order to progress atop the group.



Norway, though, must claim victory in order to pip Les Bleus to first.

That's because France have the superior goal difference, which will be taken into account should the spoils be shared in Boston.



And the winner of Group I will face a round-of-32 meeting with a third placed team from Group C, D, F, G, or H.

2 A round-of-16 showdown awaits either Norway or France Credit: Getty

The team that finishes second, meanwhile, will face the runner up from Group E.

To the uninitiated, this is the group that features both Germany and Ivory Coast.



Germany will progress as group winners in Group E and face a third-placed team from Groups A, B, C, D or F.

However, should Germany win their round-of-32 tie, then they would take on the winner of the tie between the Group I winner and a third placed team from Group C, D, F, G, or H in the round-of-16.

As things stand, that may see France face Germany in the last-16 of the World Cup should Didier Deschamps' side claim a result against Norway on Friday.

It would be a clash between two of Europe's powerhouse sides in their bid to win the World Cup in North America.

Sports.title: Championship clubs make fun of Southampton after EFL fixture announcement
Sports.content:
Birmingham City and Wrexham fired cheeky digs at Southampton over the Spygate saga after the Championship fixtures were announced.

The Saints learned their fixture fate for the upcoming 2026/27 campaign, which kicks off in the wake of their unprecedented expulsion from last season's play-offs.

3 Southampton will come up against 'Spygate' rivals Middlesbrough again this season Credit: Getty

In the most dramatic of conclusions in English football's second tier, Tonda Eckert's side were denied a Wembley showdown with Hull City after admitting to spying on three other clubs' training sessions.

It came after an analyst was caught filming Middlesbrough's training ahead of their play-off semi-final first leg.

Southampton are now gearing up for another year in the second tier, after their hefty sanction ended their Premier League ambitions.

Their route out of the Championship will be tougher this time too, with the Saints also deducted four points from the start of the 2026/27 season by the EFL's independent disciplinary commission.

'Check training ground'

There will be plenty of eyes on Southampton in the upcoming season, who have already been given a taste of things to come.

After EFL clubs discovered their fixtures for the 2026/27 season, two of their Championship rivals wasted no time in poking fun at the south coast side over Spygate.

Birmingham begin their campaign away to Sheffield United, but highlighted their September clash with the Saints on social media.

A post from the club's official X account read: "One of the other key fixtures to keep an eye on..."

Alongside this, the Blues posted a graphic of both clubs' badges cut into grass hedges, shown through the eye of binoculars.

Another of Southampton's rivals, Wrexham, also aimed a sly dig, after missing out on the Championship's last play-off place last term.

3 One of the other key fixtures to keep an eye on… Credit: X formerly Twitter / @BCFC

3 So too did Wrexham, who were left frustrated when the Saints clinched one last season's play-off places ahead of them Credit: X formerly Twitter / @Wrexham_AFC

The Hollywood-owned outfit get their campaign underway with a Welsh derby against Cardiff on August 17, before meeting Eckert's side 18 days late.

Alongside a photo of the fixture calendar in September, Wrexham included a caption that read: 'Taking us into the international break', with an emoji of a spy holding a magnifying glass.

The graphic also included a note to 'check training ground' two days before their game with the Saints

Eagle-eyed fans would have also noticed that Southampton's crest had been edited to include a caricature of a man behind a tree.

This a reference to a leaked image of their intern, William Salt, standing behind a tree watching a training session, with images of this later spreading on social media during the scandal.

New rivalry

While plenty of teams will want to get one over Southampton, none will be more desperate than Middlesbrough.

Boro were subsequently reinstated into the play-offs but lost in the final to Hull City at Wembley Stadium.

As a result, the two sides will meet again in the second tier this term, and Sky Sports were quick to highlight the significance.

Following the fixtures' release, the broadcaster shared a graphic online outlining the dates of the league's fiercest derby clashes.

This included Millwall's clash with newly-relegated rivals West Ham, as well as Southampton's meeting with south coast adversaries Portsmouth.

Also mentioned in the post was the dates for the Saints' reunion with Boro, reflecting the new-found hostilities between the pair.

Kim Hellberg's side will have to wait a few months before they can seek revenge on Southampton though, with the two teams not facing off at St Mary's until November 28.

The reverse fixture at the Riverside will take place on March 13 of next year, as the season begins to reach the run-in stage.

Sports.title: Hyped USMNT fans shell out $1,300 per ticket just to watch Pulisic in ‘meaningless’ World Cup match
Sports.content:
World Cup fever has taken over the USA and fans are paying $1,300 just to get in the door for a meaningless match vs Turkiye on Thursday at Los Angeles Stadium.

Hyped USMNT fans shell out $1,300 per ticket just to watch Pulisic in ‘meaningless’ World Cup match

The United States is already a lock for the Round of 32.

But just because a group stage World Cup match vs Turkiye is 'meaningless' on Thursday, that doesn't mean proud USA fans won't shell out big bucks to watch Christian Pulisic and Co. in person.

3 Christian Pulisic is expected to return to USMNT action on Thursday vs Turkiye Credit: Getty

The cheapest price for a single ticket on a secondary market site just hours before kickoff was $1,231.

But that seat was near the top of Los Angeles Stadium, which has a 70,000-person capacity for the 2026 World Cup.

Mauricio Pochettino's squad started 2-0 in Group D and is expected to play Bosnia and Herzegovina in a Round of 32 knockout contest on July 1 at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium.

That venue normally hosts Brock Purdy's 49ers and recently was the site of Super Bowl LX, which was won by Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks.

With the Round of 32 match already creating a win-or-go home scenario for the US Men's National Team, there was technically nothing at stake for Thursday's Group D finale vs Turkiye -- except for American pride.

“When you defend your jersey, your flag, your culture, it’s always about pride,” Pochettino said.

“I have no doubt that the Turkish team is going to be competitive tomorrow. They have good players. Of course, they are eliminated, but I think it’s going to be a tough game. We’re not thinking that it’s going to be a game that’s going to be easy.”

USMNT opened World Cup play with a sharp 4-1 win over Paraguay, then blanked Australia 2-0.

The combined 6-1 score turned the USA into one of the hottest teams of the summer.

Pulisic is expected to return to action vs Turkiye, who is playing its final match of the World Cup.

3 USMNT fans are paying $1,300 to get in the door at Los Angeles Stadium Credit: getty

3 Mauricio Pochettino is enjoying World Cup fever in the USA Credit: getty

“I’ve been touching the ball every day, and I’ve been working a lot,” Pulisic said.

“Get a couple training sessions in, and I’ll feel ready.”

The get-in price for Curacao vs Ivory Coast on Thursday was $526, which is affordable for a World Cup ticket.

But France vs Norway cost $1,598 just to get into Boston Stadium, while Portugal vs Colombia on Saturday was a whopping $3,035 to walk through the gate.

USMNT's Chris Richards, Antonee Robinson, Tyler Adams and Folarin Balogun all have lingering yellow cards from earlier matches.

A second yellow would result in a one-game suspension.

Pochettino said it would be an “unnecessary risk” to use those players vs Turkiye, which means that fans are willing to pay almost $1,500 to watch a USMNT squad missing four of its biggest names -- and sit near the top of a huge NFL stadium.

Sports.title: Theo Walcott names his all-time World Cup XI: An all-Italian centre-back partnership, an Englishman who has never won it - and no room for Pele or Diego Maradona!
Sports.content:
Theo Walcott names his all-time World Cup XI: An all-Italian centre-back partnership, an Englishman who has never won it - and no room for Pele or Diego Maradona!

Have you paid attention to the action so far? Try our World Cup quiz HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former Arsenal star Theo Walcott has had his say on who he would pick to make up his tournament’s all-time XI.

The winger made his national debut against Andorra 20 years ago, aged just 17 years old. Today, he still holds the record as the youngest player to have made his senior debut for England.

Walcott announced his international retirement in 2016 and has played with and against some of the finest players in the world.

Here is his greatest ever World Cup XI. What do you make of the side?

Gianluigi Buffon, Italy

After his retirement in 2023, Buffon is recognised as one of the greatest goalkeepers to have ever played the game.

The Italian shot-stopper has featured in four world cups, including the 2006 campaign where Italy lifted the Jules Rimet trophy after beating France on penalties.

He conceded just twice in seven games in that campaign and was also awarded the Lev Yashin award for best goalkeeper of the tournament.

The 48-year-old has made 176 appearances for the Azzurri, which makes him the all-time leading appearance holder.

Legendary Italy goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon makes it into Theo Walcott's all-time World Cup XI

Walcott has teamed up with Amazon to celebrate the return of Prime Day, from June 23 to 26

Cafu, Brazil

Born in Sao Paolo, two-time World Cup winner Cafu is hailed as an icon by football fans across the world.

He is the only man to have played in three World Cup finals, where he triumphed against Italy in 1994 and Germany in 2002, but fell short with Brazil after losing to France in 1998.

Cafu has been praised for his work ethic and ‘never say die’ attitude. His talent combined with his passion and love for the game are the reasons why he’s considered one of the greatest full backs ever.

Fabio Cannavaro, Italy

Cannavaro has appeared in four World Cup competitions, tasting success in 2006 alongside Gianluigi Buffon.

After leading Juventus to a Serie A title just weeks before his World Cup winning campaign, he became just the third defender in history to have won the Ballon d’Or award.

The Italians nicknamed him ‘Il Muro di Berlino’ (the Berlin Wall) thanks to his imposing defensive displays, despite being just 5’8.

Now, as the 2026 World Cup looms large, Cannavaro has adopted a different role. He will lead Uzbekistan out to their first global tournament in the history of the country.

Captain Cafu steered Brazil to World Cup glory in 2002, having already tasted success in 1994

Fabio Cannavaro guided Italy to a stunning 2006 World Cup triumph, winning the Ballon d'Or

Paolo Maldini, Italy

After making his debut for the Italian national team in 1988, Maldini spent 14 years serving his country. He made an appearance at four different World Cups but never won the trophy.

In 1994 he won his third Champions League title and finished as runner up with Italy in the World Cup.

His performances at both club and international level were so monstrous that he became the first defender ever to win World Soccer magazine’s annual World Player of the Year award.

He is regarded as one of the best defenders of all time, thanks to his supreme reading of the game, talent on both feet and sheer physicality.

Ashley Cole, England

At left back, Walcott opted for his former teammate Ashley Cole who has featured consistently in a number of Premier League all time XIs.

Cole played at five major tournaments for England including three World Cups in 2002, 2006 and 2010. He has made 107 appearances for England and is one of the most capped defenders in his nation’s history. He set a record for going 34 consecutive home appearances without defeat for England.

Cole was also named in the team of the Tournament for the 2004 Euros. Walcott dubbed his ex-teammate as “the best left-back in Premier League history” when speaking to FourFourTwo, which is a statement many would find hard to disagree with. Cole slots in to make up a formidable defensive unit.

His team-mate Paolo Maldini completes an all-Italian centre-back partnership in Walcott's XI

Ashley Cole is the only Englishman to make Walcott's XI, having starred at three World Cups

Claude Makelele, France

Onto the midfield, and Makelele pins down the first spot as the engine of the team. He has featured at two World Cups in 2002 and 2006.

Makelele revolutionised the role of a midfielder, dictating a lot of matches with his playmaking from a deep position.

He had incredible defensive awareness and his performances in the 2006 World Cup showcased this, as France reached the final but were beat by Italy.

Makelele is lauded for his impressive physicality and elite understanding of his role on the pitch. He is widely appreciated as one of the greatest French players ever.

Xavi, Spain

Xavi featured at four World Cups during his international career, making 133 appearances in 14 years. He won the FIFA World Youth Championship with Spain in 1999 and 11 years later got his hands on the World Cup trophy after the Spaniards defeated the Dutch.

In the 2010 World Cup he racked up an incredible passing accuracy of 91%, providing the most accurate passes, with 599, in the tournament.

He was named the Euro 2008’s player of the tournament and led Spain to their first bit of silverware since 1964. In 2012 he picked up two assists in Spain’s 4-0 thrashing of Italy to help retain the European Championship for his country.

France legend Claude Makelele (right) revolutionised the role of a defensive midfielder

Xavi was brilliant during Spain's 2010 World Cup success, boasting the most accurate passes

Zinedine Zidane, France

Next is a man that needs no introduction in Zinedine Zidane.

In 1998 he won the World Cup final against Brazil, scoring two headers in the first half to put the game beyond doubt.

In 2006 he starred in France’s run to the final, with the captain scoring goals against Spain in the round of 16 and Portugal in the semifinals.

A scintillating performance against Brazil in the campaign showed the world why Zidane was one of the best players on the planet.

He scored in the final against Italy from the penalty spot before a headbutt to Marco Materazzi’s chest ended the Frenchman’s involvement. This moment has become one of the most infamous moments in World Cup history.

Zidane scored 31 goals and picked up 29 assists in 108 games.

Lionel Messi, Argentina

After claiming the trophy, he had been chasing all his life at the last campaign in Qatar, Messi looks set to play in his final World Cup in North America this summer.

The little magician was involved in ten of Argentina’s 15 goals at the last tournament in 2022. The two-time Copa America winner has scored 117 goals and provided 64 assists in an illustrious 199 game international career.

Messi’s impact on his teammates was clear to see in Qatar. He was treated as a king, and the Argentinian squad put their bodies on the line for their captain.

His reputation speaks for itself.

Zinedine Zidane inspired France to World Cup glory in 1998 and nearly prevailed again in 2006

Lionel Messi is continuing to take the World Cup by storm this year after winning it in 2022

Ronaldo Nazario, Brazil

Ronaldo Nazario made his debut for the Selecao in 1994. He went on to score 62 goals in 99 appearances for Brazil.

‘O Fenomeno’ was pivotal to Brazil’s success, winning two World Cups in 1994 and 2002, scoring a brace against Germany in the final of the latter.

Ronaldo’s explosive pace, ridiculous skillset and incredible ability to punish teams is what renders him as one of the greatest strikers ever.

Despite his injuries and time out on the sidelines Ronaldo Nazario goes down as one of the deadliest strikers of all time.

Cristiano Ronaldo, Portugal

In his 23rd year of international football, Cristiano Ronaldo has recorded the most international appearances, with 227, and the most goals at international level with 143.

Portugal won the 2016 European Championship final against France, in what was a day of mixed emotions for the Portugal captain.

An injury in the first half of the game forced him to be subbed off with the forward visibly distressed. But that did not stop him adopting a player-manager role on the bench, guiding Portugal to their first ever piece of silverware.

The 41-year-old will take on his sixth World Cup campaign joined by Messi and Guillermo Ochoa as the only players to have featured at six or more global tournaments.

As always, all the talk surrounds him as he looks to secure the one trophy that has evaded him his whole career.

Ronaldo Nazario was pivotal to Brazil winning two World Cups in 1994 and 2002

All-time great Cristiano Ronaldo is the only player in football history to score at six World Cups

Do you agree with Walcott's XI?

Pick your XI from the shortlist and submit your final selection.

You can then compare it to our Daily Mail football experts.

You can also share your team with your friends and see how your selection compares with thousands of other Mail readers…

Sports.title: Max Verstappen in secret talks with McLaren over sensational switch from Red Bull: £80m-a-year star could move as early as next year, with Oscar Piastri going the other way
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen and McLaren have opened preliminary talks with a view to partnering the Dutchman and Lando Norris in a dream team of world champions.

It is understood that in this scenario Norris's existing partner Oscar Piastri would swap places with the Dutchman if the hush-hush negotiations ended in a successful resolution, possibly as early as next year.

Verstappen has been considering his future for some time, with Red Bull's form having dropped off since their title-winning exploits between 2021 and 2014.

The four-time world champion has traditionally been in no rush to sever his ties with the Austria-owned organisation that have nurtured his talent, placing loyalty high in his thoughts.

Nor has McLaren chief executive Zak Brown publicly courted Vertstappen, though the American sounded him out a couple of years ago, only to be assured the services of Formula One's most sought-after driver were unavailable.

Verstappen is contracted to Red Bull until the end of 2028, but certain release clauses allow him to move earlier should he wish to activate them. He is likely to keep his options open for as long as possible to assess how the top teams develop under the current regulations that are only seven races old.

Max Verstappen could line up alongside Lando Norris (right) at McLaren if talks are successful

On the other side of the equation, Verstappen has toyed with the idea of quitting Formula One, a consideration that gained impetus as the 28-year-old railed against the controversial move to the half-electric engines - an unsatisfactory combination he believes has reduced racing to the status of a 'Mario Kart' computer game. He lies seventh in the drivers' standings, 101 points behind Mercedes' leader Kimi Antonelli.

However, it is understood McLaren believe they stand a chance of luring their man, whose annual pay at Red Bull is some £80million.

'It is an idea McLaren are keen on,' confirmed one source. 'If it comes off it may be in 2028, but it could even be earlier.'

A pathway to Verstappen has been opened by McLaren's signing of his key lieutenant, his long-serving race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase, known as 'GP'.

The British-Italian is on a long stretch of gardening leave after his departure from Red Bull in April and will join McLaren - at the latest - when his contract expires in 2028.

Verstappen has always considered 'GP' a cornerstone of his Red Bull existence. Another trusted figure in his existence there was Dr Helmut Marko, the soft-drink manufacturer's motorsport adviser, but the octogenarian left the company last year.

Whatever the result of the Verstappen-McLaren dance, George Russell feels his place at Mercedes is entirely safe.

Although Verstappen has regularly been linked with Russell's seat, the Englishman issued an adamant assessment ahead of Sunday's Austrian Grand Prix, insisting: 'I'll be racing here next year.

'I don't want to go into any more detail, but I will be at Mercedes in 2027 and that's the fact of it.'

Sports.title: Cole Palmer breaks his silence on World Cup axe - and says he'll only watch England's matches 'if I'm not doing anything' and 'I'm not crying over a decision you can't change'
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer breaks his silence on World Cup axe - and says he'll only watch England's matches 'if I'm not doing anything' and 'I'm not crying over a decision you can't change'

Have you paid attention to the action so far? Try our World Cup quiz HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Cole Palmer has insisted he is 'not crying' over Thomas Tuchel's decision to axe him from England's World Cup squad this summer - but says he won't pay close attention to their progress.

The Chelsea star, 24, appeared to have carved out a long-term future with the national team after impressively bursting on to the scene at Stamford Bridge and scoring in England's Euro 2024 final against Spain, but an unprecedented dip in form has seen him fall out of Tuchel's plans completely.

The German's decision to omit Palmer, as well as Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold and Manchester City star Phil Foden, came as a huge surprise to several fans and will remain a talking point if England continue to struggle in attacking areas as they did during their disappointing 0-0 draw against Ghana.

But Palmer, who has now been forced into taking a rare summer break, is eager to look at the positives.

'I'm going to relax this summer, rest for the first time in three or four years, before getting back to what I love,' he told i-D during an interview titled Cole Palmer, The Abnormally Normal One.

'This season hasn't been the best, but it is what it is. I'm not crying over a decision you can't change, and I hope the lads make it all the way.'

Axed Cole Palmer says he will only watch England at the World Cup 'if I'm not doing anything'

Palmer is pictured with his girlfriend Olivia Holder while on holiday in Ibiza this summer

Asked if he will watch England closely in the United States, Canada and Mexico this summer, he said: 'If I'm not doing anything, then I'll watch the matches, yeah.'

Palmer enjoyed a sensational debut season with Chelsea following his transfer from Manchester City in 2023, scoring 22 goals and assisting 11 in 33 Premier League appearances that campaign.

Rewarded with a Three Lions call-up by Gareth Southgate in the summer, Palmer played a key role off the bench for England en route to the final, where he scored a stunning equaliser as a substitute before Spain's heartbreaking late winner.

The following 2024-25 season, while less emphatic, was still fruitful for Palmer as he took on the responsibility of being Chelsea's new main man, contributing 15 goals and nine assists in the Premier League that term.

But last campaign saw Palmer's form fall drastically below his usual standards, as he was forced to manage a string of frustrating injuries in his groin and later hamstring.

Playing in just 26 Premier League appearances, he managed only 10 goals and one assist as Chelsea endured a nightmare second half of the campaign, finishing 10th and falling entirely out of European football.

During his time away from the England camp this summer, Palmer has been busy holidaying and relaxing with his girlfriend Olivia Holder.

The Chelsea star was first spotted at Wayne Lineker's O Beach Club in Ibiza days after the end of the Premier League season, posing up a storm with Gary's party impresario brother.

Relaxing over the summer is proving a welcomed silver lining for Palmer after his England axe

Palmer then returned to the White Isle with another group for a second trip to Spain in mid-June, as his sister, influencer Hallie Jennifer Palmer, shared a picture of her brother travelling in modest circumstances, with the family opting to hop on a Jet2 flight to reach their destination.

He and Holder were pictured embracing in a swimming pool while basking in the Spanish sun.

For Palmer, escaping football's rigorous and intense environment helps him to cool off, and spending more time with friends and family this summer has been a welcomed silver lining.

'I don't get too down,' he added. 'I just talk to my friends outside of football. They're normal people, so it helps me feel normal, feel grounded.'

Sports.title: Latest on Tottenham's pursuit of Mateus Fernandes amid interest from Man United - as Craig Bellamy's Burnley move stalls: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Onana closing in on United exit

Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana is close to agreeing a second loan to Turkish side Trabzonspor.

Leeds increase offer for Charles

Leeds have made an improved bid for Southampton midfielder Shea Charles worth up to £25million.

The Elland Road club had their first offer rejected at the weekend and have returned with an increase as they try to secure the Northern Ireland international.

Leeds have already agreed a four-year contract for free agent Harry Wilson, formerly of Fulham, and want Borussia Dortmund's Julian Brandt too.

They continue to work on adding goalkeepers and need a centre back.

Southampton, meanwhile, are in advanced talks with former Sunderland midfielder Dan Neil. The free agent, who was on loan at Ipswich Town, is close to signing for Tonda Eckhart.

Wolves and West Ham are also interested in the 24-year-old.

Kinsky closes in on new deal

Antonin Kinsky is closing on a new five year contract to cap a remarkable turnaround to his Tottenham career.

The 23-year-old was embarrassed by interim manager Igor Tudor last season when he was substituted following mistakes against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Questions were raised about what it would do to his mental state and whether he had a future at the club.

But, after gaining a second chance when Guglielmo Vicario required hernia surgery, the Czech has not looked back and played a huge role in keeping Spurs up.

Antonin Kinsky is set to sign a new five-year deal with Spurs

He also sacrificed his place in the Czech Republic World Cup squad to undergo a minor medical procedure and ensure his long-term fitness.

Manager Roberto de Zerbi is ready to hand him the number one starting spot next season with new signing Martin Dubravka adding competition.

Vicario is still expected to leave for Italy with Napoli and Juventus among those interested.

But for Kinsky the future looks remarkably different.

Talks over his deal are at the final stages and confirmation is expected soon.

The offer from Spurs also includes an option to extend the deal for a further year to 2032.

Cherries give veteran keeper new deal

Bournemouth have handed 38-year-old goalkeeper Fraser Forster a new one year contract.

Forster told afcb.co.uk: 'I'm pleased to be staying for another year at AFC Bournemouth.

'I've enjoyed my six months here and look forward to seeing what the group can achieve together going forwards.'

Head of football operations, Tiago Pinto, said: 'He is a key part of our dressing room. We're really pleased to be keeping Fraser here for the upcoming season.

‘His experience and contributions with his fellow goalkeepers last season were invaluable, and we look forward to seeing how they progress as a group again over the upcoming campaign.’

Gunners continue Monga talks

Arsenal are continuing talks with Leicester City over a deal for winger Jeremy Monga.

16-year-old Jeremy Monga is a target for Arsenal this summer

The 16-year-old is valued around £10m and is expected to sign a three-year professional deal with the Gunners when he turns 17 next month, prior to linking up with the first team for pre-season.

Monga also had interest from Manchester United and Newcastle but has been set on a move to the Premier League champions.

Bees keen on Flemming - as Burnley's Bellamy move stalls

Brentford are showing interest in Burnley forward Zian Flemming.

The 27-year-old scored 11 goals in the Premier League last season.

Fiorentina, meanwhile, are exploring a deal for Burnley winger Luca Koleosho, who spent last season on loan at Espanyol and Paris FC.

Meanwhile, Burnley's proposed move to make Craig Bellamy their new manager is back in the balance and they are talking to other candidates with Rob Edwards and Steve Cooper in contention.

Spurs ready to battle United for Fernandes

Tottenham are making a concerted effort to beat Manchester United to the signing of Mateus Fernandes from West Ham.

Tottenham's arrival at negotiations is helping West Ham to push for their asking price of £85million.

Mateus Fernandes is attracting attention from Tottenham and Man United this summer

Spurs have attempted to be aggressive in this summer window in their bid to strengthen Roberto De Zerbi's squad. They have not been deterred by West Ham's demands and there was increasing optimism on Wednesday that they could agree a deal.

Manchester United are mindful of paying over the odds for the 21-year-old despite his obvious potential. They do have other options but remain in talks for the Portugal international as it stands.

Spurs want Fernandes as well as Sandro Tonali from Newcastle United for their midfield. They had a £75m bid rejected for Tonali last week and plan another offer soon.

Earlier on Wednesday, they agreed to sign goalkeeper Martin Dubravka on a free transfer.

The 37-year-old Slovakian international is another defensive reinforcement following the signings of Marcos Senesi, Andy Robertson - also on free transfers from Bournemouth and Liverpool - and Netherlands defender Jan Paul van Hecke, who cost £52m from Brighton.

Tigers make move for Raskin

Hull have made an offer for Rangers and Belgium midfielder Nicolas Raskin of around £12.5million.

The 25-year-old still has two years left on contract and is valued around £20m.

Sports.title: I'm A Celeb winner AngryGinge confronts 'racist' England fan at the World Cup - and complains 'clothing brand owner' wasn't kicked out even after he reported his abuse
Sports.content:
I'm A Celeb winner AngryGinge confronts 'racist' England fan at the World Cup - and complains 'clothing brand owner' wasn't kicked out even after he reported his abuse

Have you paid attention to the action so far? Try our World Cup quiz HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

AngryGinge has hit out at the standard of stewarding at the World Cup after reporting a fan for alleged racism during England's match with Ghana on Tuesday in Foxborough, USA.

AngryGinge, real name Morgan Burtwistle - who is a YouTuber and won last year's I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! - took to social media to expose a supporter who was racist towards the Ghana players during the 0-0 draw.

It is unclear if the unidentified person in question is an England fan, but he was sitting among some Three Lions supporters.

'We have a situation where the gentleman that is sat there is being racist [points to an empty seat in front of him],' Burtwistle says in his MoreGinge YouTube video.

'I've reported it to the steward because, kick it out is the saying, I will stand by that. So he's going now getting his supervisor and we'll see what happens. There's no way he should ever set foot at a stadium or watch a football game ever again.'

A message then flashes up on screen reading: 'The man sat in front was making incredibly racist comments toward the Ghanaian national team. Due to this it was only right for me to stand up and deal with this.'

After initially being told that no action can be taken unless he says it again, Burtwistle, 24, informs his followers that due to his complaints a team is now gathering to kick the man out.

AngryGinge encountered an alleged racist fan during England's 0-0 World Cup draw vs Ghana

AngryGinge, real name Morgan Burtwistle, took to social media to expose the fan at the match

The fan apologised and asked if he could forget about it, to which Burtwistle firmly said no

'Apparently, the steward said he can't kick him out unless he does it again. I said there's no way on earth. All of us have heard it. He's got to go. So we're getting a team to kick him out now or something.'

As well as the incident, Burtwistle's incredulity grows after being asked by the perpetrator to promote his brand.

'He tried to get me to do a video to promote his brand as well. I'll try and find the name of the brand, it's run by a racist. So, we'll try to expose everything we can.'

Following Burtwistle's actions, the perpetrator can be seen apologising for his remark.

'I'm sorry about my comment about Ghana, it won't happen again,' he tells Burtwistle - who is sitting one row behind him.

'No it won't happen again,' retorted Burtwistle, 'Because you're going to get thrown out.'

Fearing that outcome, the fan asks: 'Can we just forget about it?' to which Burtwistle replies: 'Forget about you being racist!? No, mate.'

The fan is eventually kicked out of his seat but somehow stayed and watched the match elsewhere inside the stadium, according to Burtwistle.

Burtwistle in the video also complained by the actions of the American stewards in handling it

The 24-year-old won ITV's longstanding show I'm a Celebrity ... Get Me Out of Here! last year

And upon leaving the ground himself, a fuming Burtwistle, condemned the American stewards for their actions as he left the stadium by concluding his video with: 'It's absolutely not good enough from the American stewards, the message before the game the message is kick it out - if you see it, say it.

'I've gone and reported it, he's not been kicked out of the stadium, we saw him as we left, he's been allowed to watch the whole game after the things he was saying about the Ghana team.

'I think it's an absolute f***ing disgrace he's been allowed to stay in after I had the evidence and five witnesses heard him say it.

'It's an absolute f***ing disgrace, it's wrong on every single level that he can stay and get away with it. I did my part, I couldn't have done any more.'

Sports.title: Sky Sports reporter Rachel Brookes QUITS after revealing 'horrendous' abuse she suffered for viral interview with F1's Max Verstappen
Sports.content:
Sky Sports reporter Rachel Brookes QUITS after revealing 'horrendous' abuse she suffered for viral interview with F1's Max Verstappen

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Rachel Brookes has confirmed she has quit her role as a reporter for Sky Sports ahead of the Austrian Grand Prix, days after revealing 'utterly horrendous' abuse she received following an interview with Max Verstappen.

Brookes, 51, has been part of Sky Sports coverage over the past 14 years, interviewing drivers before and after races.

The reporter revealed on social media that she has now stepped away from her role.

Brookes confirmed her plan is to remain involved in Formula One and will be in attendance at Silverstone for the British Grand Prix in July despite leaving Sky.

'After many years at Sky I am moving on to exciting new ventures and looking forward to what comes next,' Brookes wrote.

'I have left the Sky F1 team but F1 still has my heart & so I'll still be involved in it.

Rachel Brookes has confirmed she has left her role as a reporter on Sky Sports F1 coverage

Brookes revealed this week she had received 'horrific abuse' from fans after an interview with Max Verstappen last year

'I'll keep you posted, in the meantime see you at Silverstone!'

Brookes, who has written the book 'F1 Racing: Drive: The Secrets to Formula One Success', revealed earlier this week the extent of the abuse she had received following an interview with Verstappen last year.

She had spoken to the four-time world champion after the Spanish Grand Prix last May.

Verstappen had been handed a 10-second penalty at the race having collided with Mercedes' George Russell.

After former world champion Nico Rosberg suggested on commentary that Verstappen may have deliberately collided with his rival, Brookes put it to the Dutchman on camera.

Brookes told the Road to Success podcast: 'I said to Max, "Was it deliberate?". 'And his response was, "Does it matter?".

She then responded: 'Yeah, I think it does to the fans watching and to the kids'.

'I want people to see how good you are, and you make it difficult when you do stuff like that.'

Brookes revealed on the podcast that she had been privately praised by her peers in broadcasting for asking Verstappen the question, but had been targeted by 'horrific' abuse from fans.

'I got a lot of messages from people in broadcasting, in sports broadcasting, saying: "Well done for asking the question",' Brookes said.

Brookes had asked the Verstappen (right), whether he had deliberately collided with George Russell (left) at the Spanish Grand Prix

'Because nobody else in that pen that day asked him that question – and even my colleagues said they wouldn't have asked that question, because they'd have been too scared to ask it.

'But then the fans, the social media side of it, was horrendous. I got people telling me I should never be able to have children because I'm a bad example. I got the most horrific stuff you could imagine.

'And this is from a lot of these profiles with dads with kids with daughters and things like that, where you just look at it and think: "Take a step back. It's a Formula 1 race. It's sport".

'But the stuff I got sent was horrendous, utterly horrendous. So I just closed my comments.'

Verstappen, who had admitted he had made a 'mistake' post-race, ultimately dropped from fifth place to 10th at the Grand Prix.

The Dutchman would go on to miss out on the world title by just two points to Lando Norris.

Sports.title: Germany's goalkeeper row! Manuel Neuer's team-mates and World Cup winner 'call' for him to be dropped vs Ecuador for player who deserves it as a 'reward' - but Julian Nagelsmann disagrees
Sports.content:
Germany's goalkeeper row! Manuel Neuer's team-mates and World Cup winner 'call' for him to be dropped vs Ecuador for player who deserves it as a 'reward' - but Julian Nagelsmann disagrees

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Germany have seamlessly qualified for the World Cup knockout stages, but despite that there is seemingly a strong debate over one key position involving a national legend.

Germany take on Ecuador in their final Group E match on Thursday in New Jersey (9pm BST).

Whatever the result, the four-time winners will finish top of the group, having already beaten Curacao (7-1) and Ivory Coast (2-1). This is in stark contrast to 2018 and 2022 when they were eliminated from the group stages.

The Ecuador match provides Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann the rare opportunity to rotate his side and give some of his squad players valuable minutes.

One of those positions would be in goal with Oliver Baumann yet to play at the World Cup with Manuel Neuer being Nagelsmann's No 1.

Neuer's return to the starting line-up has raised some eyebrows in his homeland after retiring from international football after Euro 2024.

According to reports, some Germany players want Manuel Neuer not to play against Ecuador

Some would like to Oliver Baumann start as a 'reward' for his role in their World Cup qualifiers

In his absence, Oliver Baumann became Germany's No 1 but has since had to play second-fiddle this summer.

But with Germany already assured of a place in the last 32, Sky Sports Germany report that many players within the squad would like to see Baumann, 36, be given some minutes - considering he helped them qualify for this summer's showpiece.

'Some of the national team players would like to see Oliver Baumann start in goal against Ecuador tomorrow, and thus make his World Cup debut as a "reward" and a show of appreciation for him,' they detailed on Wednesday.

'The topic has been discussed in the dressing room in recent hours. It remains to be seen whether Julian Nagelsmann and Manuel Neuer will make it happen.'

That reported sentiment has been backed up by Mats Hummels, who was part of the 2014 World Cup winning starting XI alongside Neuer.

Hummels, who was also a team-mate of the 40-year-old's at Bayern Munich, said as a pundit for Magenta TV: 'That would certainly make headlines [not playing Neuer against Ecuador].

'I've been thinking about it myself over the last few days. Personally, I would give Oli Baumann the game.

'I don't want to interfere in any way, though. But as a reward for how he handled the situation, and as the German No 1 in recent years, it would be appropriate to give him a World Cup appearance.'

Speaking about his demotion in the build-up to the tournament, Baumann admitted he was frustrated about losing his starting spot to Neuer.

'At first, it was obviously tough,' he said. 'It didn't feel cool at all to me. But I immediately knew that I would be there for the team. I didn't even think about not coming. It's a World Cup for me too.'

However, despite those calls for Baumann to start it appears Nagelsmann will not budge on Neuer - who is currently expecting a second child with his wife Anika Bissel, 24, while his ex-wife is Nina Weiss is also pregnant with her partner.

Germany legend Neuer, 40, is expecting his second child with wife Anika Bissel, 24

In his pre-match press conference on Wednesday, Nagelsmann said goalkeeper coach Andreas Kronenberg spoke with Baumann about the decision to stick with Neuer.

'Oliver really understood,' Nagelsmann said. 'I understand completely from the human side and if we only approached it that way it would be obvious, but we have to look at the large picture.

'It's not always pleasant to make these decisions but those decisions have to be made.'

Sports.title: Tennis latest: Players launch Wimbledon protest as Novak Djokovic withdraws from tournament
Sports.content:
Tennis latest: Players launch Wimbledon protest as Novak Djokovic withdraws from tournament

Wimbledon 2026 is just around the corner and the biggest names in tennis are preparing for the Grand Slam

View 3 Images Tennis stars have planned a protest ahead of Wimbledon (Image: Daniel Kopatsch, Getty Images)

Wimbledon is just around the corner, with the world's finest tennis players preparing themselves for a fortnight of gripping competition. The legendary tournament in SW19 runs from Monday, June 29, to Sunday, July 12, with the opening matches now a few days away.

Jannik Sinner and Iga Swiatek head into Wimbledon as defending champions, while last year's runner-up Carlos Alcaraz has been ruled out with a wrist injury. Serena Williams' headline-grabbing return to singles competition is another hot topic.

With the main draw for both the men's and women's singles scheduled for this Friday morning, several leading players have been sharpening their games through practice sessions and exhibition matches. Mirror Sport brings you a full round-up of the biggest talking points ahead of the Grand Slam.

Wimbledon protest planned

A cohort of leading tennis stars have confirmed they will scale back their media obligations for the opening week of Wimbledon in an act of protest. Players including Sinner, Coco Gauff and Aryna Sabalenka mounted a similar demonstration during the French Open media day last month.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

However, they are poised to take further action at the All England Club, with the planned protest running from Monday, June 29, through to Sunday, July 5. Players have been calling for a bigger slice of revenue, allocated through prize money and contributions to welfare programmes, alongside a more influential voice in decisions that impact them.

BBC make announcement about Wimbledon coverage days after losing key star READ MORE :

Andy Murray doubles down on taking BBC Wimbledon job after surprising new career change READ MORE :

The All England Club recently announced a substantial £10.7million, or 20 per cent, increase in prize money for this year's Championships, pushing the overall pot to £64.2m. Yet this elite player group has highlighted that this equates to prize money representing roughly a 14.4 per cent share of revenue, falling short of the 22 per cent they are pursuing.

They will therefore "limit their contractual media commitments at the tournament to 15 minutes - reflecting that Wimbledon currently pays slightly below 15 per cent of revenues to players as prize money - for the duration of the first week of the Championships."

Djokovic pulls out

Novak Djokovic recently pulled out of an exhibition match against Karen Khachanov, sparking fresh doubts over his fitness ahead of Wimbledon this summer. The Serbian great has made a tradition of featuring in the Giorgio Armani Tennis Classic each year as part of his build-up to the third Grand Slam of 2026.

View 3 Images Novak Djokovic withdrew from an event (Image: DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images)

However, the 24-time Grand Slam champion withdrew without providing any reason ahead of Wednesday's event. Khachanov subsequently faced and lost to American Martin Damm.

Djokovic is the No. 7 seed at Wimbledon and continues his quest to turn back the years, but has not competed since falling to Joao Fonseca in the third round of Roland Garros. That suggests he is giving his body sufficient time to fully recuperate and to preserve his fitness for the majors. However, he was seen practising at Wimbledon on Wednesday morning, indicating he remains on course to compete in next week's tournament.

Sinner returns Wimbledon trophy

Sinner has ceremonially handed back the Wimbledon men's singles trophy to the All England Club as he prepares to defend his crown. The Italian was presented with the 139-year-old trophy on Centre Court a year ago for the first time in his career.

View 3 Images Jannik Sinner won Wimbledon last year (Image: Getty)

The 24-year-old was not permitted to retain the original, and it was ceremonially returned this week. The All England Club paid 100 guineas to acquire the current silver-gilt cup in 1887 and introduced a new rule that same year.

Article continues below

The cup would remain the club's permanent possession, and future champions would be given a replica. Once the championship concludes, the actual trophy is returned to the Wimbledon Lawn Tennis Museum.

The champion's name is engraved on the silverware straight after their victory and they can parade it at the Champions Dinner that same evening. Once returned, replicas are then distributed. These were brought in during 1949 and stand at 13.5 inches tall, in contrast to the 18-inch authentic trophy.

Sports.title: Scotland fan who flew 4,000 miles to watch his team lose 3-0 on a TV screen says it was 'worth every penny'
Sports.content:
Scotland fan who flew 4,000 miles to watch his team lose 3-0 on a TV screen says it was 'worth every penny'

Neil McKnight, who is a Scotland superfan, flew 4,000 miles to watch his country lose 3-0 to Brazil on a TV screen - but he says it was "worth every penny"

View 3 Images Neil McKnight is pictured in Scotland

The Scotland superfan who flew to the United States to watch his team lose 3-0 on a TV screen insists the trip was worth “every penny”

‌



Neil McKnight couldn’t get a ticket for the game against Brazil. But he was so desperate to be part of the Tartan Army he forked out over £1000 to fly to Miami in a 70-hour trip.

‌



Speaking to the Mirror, the Ayr United fanatic said: “I’ve had a fantastic time. It’s really been worth every penny. We may have lost 3-0 but it’s been a great experience. Both sets of fans were amazing and to be part of the Tartan Army for a World Cup was brilliant. It didn’t really matter that I didn’t get a ticket for the game.

‌



"The atmosphere in the Fanfest, the bars and throughout the city was something I will always remember."

View 3 Images Scotland fans pictured in Miami (Image: CRISTOBAL HERRERA-ULASHKEVICH/EPA/Shutterstock)

Neil, 62, from Ayr, now lives in Sawbridgeworth, Herts. He laughed: "But it’s time to head back home now and by early next week I’ll be watching the World Cup back in my local - The Bull - but it won’t quite be the same!”

‌



The retired programme manager saw his first Ayr United game against Morton in 1969 and Scotland in 1982.. He has seen Scotland play at Hampden Park many times but has never travelled to watch them overseas.

He stayed in an AirBnB in the Miami suburb Little Havana. And to keep costs down he is flying back to London via Charlotte rather than direct.

View 3 Images Scotland superfan Neil McKnight who flew to Miami to watch side lose 3-0 on TV screen

‌



Before the match, Neil told Mirror online: “I’ve had a dream of watching Scotland in the World Cup ever since the Argentina tournament back in 1978.

“But tickets are so expensive and difficult to get so I decided to take the plunge and just head over.

“My wife Alison thinks it’s great I’m going."

Article continues below

His close friend England and QPR fan, Andy Clayden, laughed: “It was a long way to go and a lot of money to watch Scotland lose 3-0.”

Sports.title: Man Utd eye shock transfer for Scotland World Cup star after Brazil heartbreak
Sports.content:
Man Utd eye shock transfer for Scotland World Cup star after Brazil heartbreak

One of Manchester United's priorities for the summer transfer window is to sign a new second-choice goalkeeper, as Michael Carrick plans to bring in an experienced backup to Senne Lammens

View 2 Images Angus Gunn is a target for Manchester United (Image: Michael Pimentel/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Manchester United have added Scotland star Angus Gunn to their shortlist for a new second-choice goalkeeper. Gunn, 30, started all three of Scotland's group matches at the World Cup, despite being released by Nottingham Forest earlier this summer.

‌



The shot-stopper only made a solitary appearance during his one-year stay at the City Ground and is available on a free transfer. United's search for a new backup to Senne Lammens has led them to identity Gunn as a target.

‌



A report from the Sun states that United are eyeing a move for the 30-year-old, who came through Manchester City's academy when United director of football Jason Wilcox was a coach and then its head. Gunn left City in 2018 following a loan spell with Norwich, the same team his dad, Bryan, was playing for when Angus was born.

‌



After three years at Southampton, Gunn joined Norwich on a permanent basis. The Scotland international was released last summer and picked up by Forest.

In spite of his lack of game time for Forest, Gunn remained his country's No.1. But he was unable to help Steve Clarke's side accumulate more than three points at the World Cup, and because of their minus three goal difference - having lost 3-0 to Brazil on Wednesday - they're unlikely to finish the group stage as one of the eight best third-placed teams.

‌



Gunn would almost certainly warm the bench again if he joined United, with Lammens having enjoyed a superb first season. Altay Bayindir served as No.2 last season while Andre Onana was sent out on loan, but the Red Devils plan to sell both goalkeepers.

With Radek Vitek's future also uncertain following an impressive campaign on loan at Bristol City, 40-year-old Tom Heaton isn't seen as a suitable understudy for Lammens. Another goalkeeper on United's radar is Leeds' Karl Darlow.

Midfield is Michael Carrick's top priority for the summer transfer window, although the Red Devils look set to miss out on two of their top targets. Elliot Anderson has been priced at an obscene £130million, a fee which United are reportedly unwilling to pay.

Sports.title: Peter Crouch anthem crowned funniest UK football chant - beating Neil Diamond and Fat Les
Sports.content:
Peter Crouch anthem crowned funniest UK football chant - beating Neil Diamond and Fat Les

A Peter Crouch anthem hailing the former England player's towering height has been crowned the nation's funniest football chant - beating Neil Diamond and Fat Les to the top spot.

View 3 Images A Peter Crouch anthem hailing his towering height has been crowned the nation's funniest football chant

'He's tall, he's red, his feet stick out the bed, Peter Crouch' bagged the top spot among footy fans, narrowly squeezing Neil Diamond's Sweet Caroline into second place.

‌



Fat Les' 1998 smash hit Vindaloo rounded out the top three, taking the last spot on the podium in the research by Stonegate Group.

‌



But it's not just the classics proving to be terrace favourites, with newer chants like 'Rice, Rice baby' and tongue-in-cheek tributes to Harry Maguire keeping fans laughing.

‌



The chant culture isn't confined to the stands either, with half of fans admitting they've belted out football songs in both the pub and the stadium (52%), while a further 30% have joined in at family gatherings.

From parties (21%) and holidays (16%) to work (10%), public transport (9%) and even weddings (4%), the data shows football fever can strike almost anywhere. But when it comes to bringing that same energy home the nation is split.

View 3 Images Football fans watching England

‌



Of the 2,000 English and Scottish Football fans quizzed, 36% say they sing along often or very often while watching from the sofa, while an equal 36% admit they rarely or never join in.

The research comes ahead of Stonegate Group's 'Roar of the Nation' challenge, in partnership with Heineken, who will also be running competitions through Stonegate's loyalty app MixR.

This will take place across venues in England and Scotland, including The Minories in London, The Moot Hall Arms in Leeds and the Akenside Traders in Newcastle.

‌



The initiative encourages fans to cheer as loudly as they can during Scotland and England's fixtures, with pubs competing live against venues to be crowned the home of the loudest and most passionate supporters.

New sound data from Stonegate Group places The Minories in London as the noisiest venue in the UK after it logged an ear splitting 133.9dB during England’s opening game.

The almighty roar was recorded during the celebrations following Rashford's cleanly plucked goal, the fourth for England. At 133.9dB, this is as loud as a jet engine taking off (130-140dB) and louder than an ambulance siren or even the bone-rattling cacophony of a pneumatic drill (both 120-130).

‌



View 3 Images Peter Crouch (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

This puts England ahead of Scotland in the loudness league. Scotland have so far managed to clock 121.6dB at Chanter in Edinburgh after McGinn's thunderous opener against Haiti.

Kay Bartlett, Chief Marketing Officer at Stonegate Group, said: "Football tournaments are all about shared moments, atmosphere and traditions.

‌



"There's nothing quite like watching a huge match and enjoying the experience surrounded by fellow fans in a packed pub. Our Roar of the Nation campaign will allow us to measure the atmosphere in pubs across England and Scotland during the World Cup to see where the loudest fans and experiences of the tournament can be enjoyed."

Craig Woolley, Marketing Activation Director at HEINEKEN UK, said: "Nothing beats the buzz of the pub when our home teams are playing.

"From the first chant to the final whistle, it's where fans come together to share the tension, excitement and pure joy of the big occasion - and we can't wait."

‌



Top 10 football chants

1. 'He's tall, he's red, his feet stick out the bed, Peter Crouch!' - Peter Crouch

2. Sweet Caroline - Neil Diamond

3. Vindaloo - Fat Les

‌



4. 'Rice, Rice Baby' - Declan Rice

5. 'Harry Maguire, he drinks the vodka, he drinks the jaeger, his head is f*cking massive!' - Harry Maguire

6. 'Southgate you're the one, you still turn us on, football's coming home again' - Gareth Southgate

‌



7. 'Bowen's on fire and he's dating Dani Dyer ' - Jarrod Bowen

8. 'Walking in a Shearer Wonderland' - Alan Shearer

9. ' Jordan Pickford's got tiny arms' - Jordan Pickford

‌



10. 'Jamie Vardy's having a party' - Jamie Vardy

Regardless, UFC 329 is filled with many mouthwatering match-ups, including Cory Sandhagen's dust-up with Mario Bautista. Britain's Lone'er Kavanagh will look to continue his rise up the flyweight rankings when he takes on former 125lb title challenger Brandon Royval. Completing the main card is a jaw-dropping bout between King Green and Terrance McKinney. Pimblett's team-mate Luke Riley is also on the card and will trade leather with Kai Kamaka III on the prelims.

Article continues below

But many will be intrigued to see how McGregor fares on his return. The 37-year-old is confident he will be able to defeat his rival for a second time and remain active in the cage. "It's going to be a demolition. I know the damage he has taken. I know I will just have to touch him, and after that, it will be clinical. A win alone is not just enough. It must be spectacular and that is what it will be," he recently revealed to former American football star Nate Burleson.

On whether Holloway is a different fighter since their first meeting, he said: "Is he really? I do not really see it. I do not really see vast improvements. "In fact, the improvements he made, was after the fight he had with me where he adopted some of my moves. Then what did he do? He went on to win the world title. I son'd Max when I fought him last and I plan on doing the same again in more devastating fashion."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
